For two pulses A,B direct symbolic multiplication gives BA−AB=((a²−b²)/(ab))sin(aτ_a)sin(bτ_b) diag(1,−1), annihilated by (1,1)·diag(1,−1)·(1,1)^T. When both histories remain finite throughout exposure, terminal z>0, so the equal threshold numerators force the same x+1 sign and terminal basin. Appending a third C yields signed difference ((a²−b²)/(ab))sin angles (c+c^{-1})sin(cτ_c), generically nonzero; independently reproduced via symbolic sympy. At a=2,b=1/2,c=1 with each tangent angle 1/2, exact finite histories give terminal −6/7 (recovery to +1) vs −3/2 (post-exposure escape), with all one-pulse outcomes >−1 and no forcing-window poles. Exact post-pulse x′=1−x² basin threshold is x=−1. No claim is made about reorderings with a pole during forcing.
